mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past month predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as lower rates reduce discount rates applied to equity cash flows during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE rises above 4.5% by at least 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in housing starts (HOUST) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals sector-specific demand-supply misalignment, causing market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% MoM and INDPRO falls > 0.2% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST rises > 0.5% MoM and INDPRO falls > 0.2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL annual inflation > 3%), a rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as aggressive tightening compresses equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where CPIAUCSL inflation > 3% annually and FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past month predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as stronger consumer spending drives corporate revenue growth and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where RSAFS rises by at least 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1.0% signals manufacturing contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as recession risks increase.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where INDPRO falls > 1.0% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals labor-demand decoupling, causing market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 0.3% MoM and HOUST falls > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises > 0.3% MoM and HOUST falls > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 quarterly growth rate 1.0-2.0%), a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals resilient consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth rate between 1.0% and 2.0%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where GDPC1 quarterly growth rate is 1.0-2.0% and HOUST rises > 0.5% MoM.
